0.headline: Crystal Crop Protection IPO GMP at 17% ahead of issue opening on November 18; check issue size, price band and key details here
0.heading: Crystal Crop Protection IPO GMP at 17% ahead of issue opening on November 18; check issue size, price band and key details here
0.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of Crystal Crop Protection is commanding a grey market premium (GMP) of nearly 17 percent ahead of its subscription opening on November 18.
0.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of Crystal Crop Protection is commanding a grey market premium (GMP) of nearly 17 percent ahead of its subscription opening on November 18.

In the grey market, Crystal Crop Protection IPO was trading at a premium of Rs 45 per share as of November 13, according to data from InvestorGain. This translates into a GMP of around 16.54 percent over the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 272.

Going by the latest grey market premium, the estimated listing price of Crystal Crop Protection shares stands at around Rs 317 apiece, marking a potential gain of approximately 16.5 percent over the issue price.

Read Also: Crystal Crop Protection fixes price band at Rs 259-272 per share for Rs 456-crore IPO, issue opens November 18

However, the grey market premium is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment and does not guarantee listing gains. It can fluctuate depending on market conditions and should not be considered a prediction of the actual listing price.

Crystal Crop Protection has fixed the price band for its upcoming IPO at Rs 259-272 per equity share. At the upper end of the price band, the agrochemicals company is seeking a valuation of around Rs 4,438 crore.

The company aims to raise approximately Rs 455.7 crore through the public issue, which will open for subscription on November 18 and close on November 20. The bidding for anchor investors will take place on November 17.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 354.77 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 37.03 lakh equity shares aggregating to around Rs 100.71 crore.

While the proceeds from the fresh issue will go to the company, the OFS component will allow existing shareholders to sell their stakes.

The three-day public issue will open on November 18 and close on November 20. The basis of allotment is expected to be finalised on November 23, while the initiation of refunds and credit of shares to demat accounts are scheduled for November 25.

The shares are tentatively scheduled to list on the BSE and NSE on November 26.

About Crystal Crop Protection

Established in 1994, Crystal Crop Protection is a crop solutions company headquartered in New Delhi. Its business portfolio includes agrochemicals, seeds and other agricultural solutions.

The company manufactures and markets crop protection products, including herbicides, fungicides and insecticides, along with natural crop solutions and seeds for field crops, vegetables and flowers.

1.headline: Watrana Rentals to launch Rs 120-crore IPO on November 19; sets price band at Rs 232–245
1.heading: Watrana Rentals to launch Rs 120-crore IPO on November 19; sets price band at Rs 232–245
1.intro: Watrana Rentals IPO | The public issue comprises an entirely fresh issue of 49.02 lakh shares.
1.body:
Delhi-based material handling equipment provider Watrana Rentals on Friday fixed the price band at Rs 232–245 per share for its upcoming initial public offering (IPO).

The IPO will open for public subscription on November 19 and close on November 23, while the anchor book for institutional investors will open for one day on November 18.

The company aims to raise Rs 120 crore through its maiden public issue at the upper end of the price band. The IPO comprises an entirely fresh issue of 49.02 lakh shares.

Promoted by Sanjeev Kumar Watrana and Rajeev Kumar Watrana, the company provides material handling equipment, including forklifts, reach trucks and powered pallet trucks, on a rental basis. It is also engaged in trading new and used material handling equipment, as well as batteries used in material handling equipment (MHE).

The company caters to various industries, including automotive, tyres, beverages, glass, paper, logistics and warehousing.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Watrana Rentals plans to utilise Rs 98.12 crore of the IPO proceeds to purchase material handling equipment, aerial work platforms and batteries. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes and offer-related expenses.

The IPO share allotment is expected to be finalised by November 25, while Watrana Rentals is likely to make its market debut on the NSE Emerge platform on November 27.

Financial Performance
Watrana Rentals reported a profit of Rs 7.68 crore and revenue from operations of Rs 53.5 crore for the three months ended June 2026.

The company's financial performance has also remained healthy in recent years. For the financial year ended March 2026, its profit increased 19.3 percent to Rs 29.2 crore, while revenue grew 17.8 percent to Rs 211.4 crore compared with the previous financial year.

Oneview Corporate Advisors has been appointed as the merchant banker managing the Watrana Rentals IPO.

2.headline: Agrochemicals maker Crystal Crop Protection seeks Rs 4,438-crore valuation via IPO
2.heading: Agrochemicals maker Crystal Crop Protection seeks Rs 4,438-crore valuation via IPO
2.intro: Crystal Crop Protection IPO | The company plans to raise Rs 455.7 crore through its maiden public issue, comprising a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 355 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 37.02 lakh equity shares.
2.body:
New Delhi-headquartered crop protection solutions provider Crystal Crop Protection has announced November 18 as the opening date for its upcoming initial public offering (IPO) and fixed the price band at Rs 259–272 per share.

The company plans to raise Rs 455.7 crore through its maiden public issue, comprising a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 355 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 37.02 lakh equity shares by promoter Ankur Aggarwal, amounting to Rs 100.7 crore.

At the upper end of the price band, the agrochemicals manufacturer is seeking a market capitalisation of Rs 4,438.1 crore.

Around a month ago, Crystal Crop Protection revised the IPO size, reducing the fresh issue component from Rs 600 crore to Rs 439.2 crore and halving the OFS from 74.05 lakh shares to 37.02 lakh shares. Promoters Nand Kishore Aggarwal and Komal Aggarwal, along with investors International Finance Corporation and IFC Emerging Asia Fund, also withdrew from the OFS.

Subsequently, the company undertook a private placement of equity shares, raising Rs 84.2 crore at Rs 272.07 per share. This led to a further reduction in the fresh issue size to Rs 355 crore.

The anchor book for institutional investors will open for one day on November 17, while the IPO will close for public subscription on November 20.

The company is expected to finalise the share allotment on November 23, while trading in Crystal Crop Protection shares on the BSE and NSE is scheduled to commence on November 26.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Business

Established in 1994, Crystal Crop Protection has manufacturing facilities in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Haryana and Jammu and Kashmir. Its product portfolio includes crop protection solutions such as herbicides, fungicides and insecticides; natural crop solutions such as biostimulants, bioprotectants, plant growth regulators, liquid fertilisers and micronutrients; and seeds for field crops, vegetables and flowers.

Objectives

The company intends to utilise Rs 270 crore from the net proceeds of the fresh issue towards debt repayment. The remaining proceeds will be used to pursue inorganic growth through potential acquisitions and for general corporate purposes.

As of August 2026, the company had total fund-based borrowings of Rs 962.6 crore on a consolidated basis.

Financial Performance

Crystal Crop Protection reported a profit of Rs 135.7 crore on revenue of Rs 1,197.1 crore for the three months ended June 2026.

For the financial year ended March 2026, the company's profit increased 22.4 percent to Rs 144.9 crore, while revenue rose 17.2 percent to Rs 3,152 crore compared with the previous financial year.

Shareholding

Promoter Ankur Aggarwal and family members along with their entities held 84.92 percent stake in Crystal Crop Protection, while public shareholders owned 10.35 percent shares.

International Finance Corporation and its entity IFC Emerging Asia Fund held 8.29 percent shareholding in the company, while WhiteOak Capital India Opportunities Fund picked up 1.03 percent shares in pre-IPO round.

IIFL Capital Services, DAM Capital Advisors and Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors are the merchant bankers managing the Crystal Crop Protection IPO.
